boundary_convention_testable.note: incident onsets lie on the 30 s grid and decision times on a 5 s offset of a 60 s grid, so an onset can never equal t or t+H: the (t, t+H] boundary convention cannot affect any label in this dataset

precursor_visibility_in_observed_telemet.statistic: |mean(last 10 min before onset) - mean(60-120 min before onset)| / profile noise floor sigma_marg

incident_definition_observed_levels.reading: mem_leak incidents begin when memory reaches theta in [93, 99.5] %; disk_fill when usage reaches 100 - r with r in [0.5, 5] %; cpu_runaway when utilisation/capacity >= rho_crit in [0.97, 1.10] for 150 s; net_flood when rx >= 0.85-1.0 x a capacity cap for 150 s; pool_exhaustion when the hidden pool reaches 1.0. An 'outage' is therefore a saturation event defined by the simulator, not an externally observed failure.

code_locations: backend/ml/predict.py: RiskModel._rule uses np.nan_to_num(arr[:, idx], nan=0.0) / 100.0 then max()
backend/ml/predict.py: predict_risk ends with np.nan_to_num(risk, nan=0.0, ...)
backend/ml/train_baselines.py: rule scorer lambda uses np.nan_to_num(X[:, ridx], nan=0.0).max(axis=1) / 100.0
logreg: SimpleImputer(strategy='median') fitted on train: missing is treated as a typical value, not as high or unknown risk
missing_as_zero.why_it_is_latent_in_current_metrics: Rows whose latest observation is stale or whose window coverage is low are removed as 'insufficient_data' BEFORE features are built, so in every scored train/val row cpu_mean_300, mem_last and disk_*_last are present (verified: see rule_feature_nan_in_scored_train_val_rows). The NaN->0 path is therefore never exercised by the reported metrics; it only acts at inference time when telemetry is stale or absent.

realism.scope: only structural statistics that SMD/PSM actually support; no feature mapping is made

smd_train_first_10_machines_non_constant.note: SMD sampling interval is not in the files, so lag 60 is 60 rows, not 60 minutes; no diurnal lag is tested

psm_train_all_non_constant_features.note: PSM row index steps by 1 (minute per the column name; not wall-clock), so lag 1440 is one nominal day

structural_validity.evidence: schema validation 0 failures, accounting and footprint checks in the manifest, independent re-derivation in this audit

statistical_similarity.limit: SMD/PSM have no named metrics, units or real timestamps; only generic smoothness/discreteness can be compared, and a match proves nothing about realism

temporal_realism.limit: lag-k autocorrelation can be compared; diurnal/weekly structure only in PSM and only if its index is truly minutes; incident timing cannot

causal_realism.limit: no dataset available to us records resource state before real outages; precursor-to-outage mechanisms are the simulator author's assumptions

real_world_predictive_validity.limit: needs real incident records with impact times; none exist in the repository or the external sets

code_checks.splits_requested_for_fitting_or_selectio: train, val only (SPLITS_USED = ('train', 'val'); load_view asserts split in SPLITS_USED)
code_checks.threshold_objective: maximum F1 on validation rows (not tied to the 1 false alarm / host-day budget in protocol.json)
code_checks.rows_used_for_training: positive+negative rows only; unscorable (ABRUPT/SILENT-only) windows dropped; optional negative thinning (--negative-stride)
code_checks.false_alarm_definition: alert is false iff n_in_window == 0, i.e. an alert before ANY incident incl. ABRUPT/SILENT counts as correct
code_checks.exposure_denominator: scored rows x 60 s (incl. unscorable rows)
code_checks.incident_level_recall_or_lead_time: not computed (alert_stats docstring: 'not the full match-1 event evaluation')
code_checks.calibration: not assessed (no reliability curve, Brier or ECE anywhere in train_baselines.py)
code_checks.metric_level: row (decision-point) level PR-AUC/precision/recall/F1 on adjacent 60 s rows that are near-duplicates; ~30 positive rows per incident
